sections.title: 5. Ads in the free version
paragraphs: This section applies to versions of DoseWeek that are a free download with the optional Plus subscription. Free users see ads; Plus subscribers do not. Ads are shown by the Google Mobile Ads SDK (AdMob), and ad consent is handled by Google's User Messaging Platform (UMP). Both are provided by Google. No ad is shown until Google Play has confirmed whether you have Plus. Once Plus is confirmed, the app removes ads at once and does not start the ad SDK; ad requests already sent before that moment are not recalled.

DoseWeek requests only non-personalized ads. The app removes the advertising ID permission and the Android ad-services permissions for the advertising ID, attribution and topics, and it removes the install referrer service, so the SDK reads the advertising ID as zeros. Every ad request asks for non-personalized ads.

Non-personalized ads still involve processing. When the SDK requests, shows and measures an ad, Google receives your IP address, device and app information (such as device model, operating-system version, app version and language), ad interaction data (such as views and taps), diagnostic data, identifiers the SDK creates for this app, and the app set ID, which Google Play services provides and which apps from the same developer share on the device. Google uses this information to serve ads, to limit how often an ad is shown, to prevent fraud and abuse and to measure ads. Google receives it as a recipient under its own terms and privacy policy, processes it on its servers, which can be outside your country, and keeps it for the periods Google sets; DoseWeek cannot shorten them. The data leaves the device over the internet while ads are requested, shown and measured. The developer sees only aggregated AdMob reports, such as ad views and earnings.

Where the law requires consent, for example in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, Switzerland and some US states, Google's consent message appears before any ad is requested, and ads are requested only after the SDK reports that they may be. To find out whether a message is needed, the app asks Google's consent service at launch, for Free users only; this request also reaches Google and is separate from ad requests. You can review or change your choice at any time in Settings > Privacy choices for ads; where your region needs no choice, that screen says so. The one-time notice that DoseWeek is now free with ads only informs you; reading it is not consent. If ad processing is not allowed, because you declined, the form could not load or the consent service is unavailable, DoseWeek shows no ads and every Free feature keeps working. DoseWeek for Android is still only for people aged 18 or older; the age confirmation is unchanged and separate from ad consent, usage analytics and overseas transfer.

DoseWeek never passes health records, notes, medication names, doses, dates, meals or screen names to the ad SDK, and ad requests carry no keywords, content links or custom targeting. The app's ad code does not read your records. Like any SDK, Google's SDKs run inside the app process with the same technical access to the app's files as the app itself. DoseWeek does not give them your records, but it cannot technically prevent that access, so this boundary depends on Google's SDKs behaving as Google documents them.

AdMob is not linked to Firebase or Google Analytics. Ad consent and analytics consent (section 3) are separate: neither choice grants or withdraws the other, and the analytics settings keep advertising storage, ad user data and ad personalization denied. To report an ad, tap the AdChoices icon on the ad, or use Report an ad in Settings, which opens an email to support with the time and the screen where the ad appeared. It adds no health data; please do not add any.

Ad data can be transferred outside your country. The details of this transfer are below.

Recipient: Google LLC, 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, CA 94043, USA. For people in the European Economic Area and Switzerland, Google's terms name Google Ireland Limited, Gordon House, Barrow Street, Dublin 4, Ireland. Google's privacy policy explains how to contact Google, including its data protection office: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Countries: the United States and other countries where Google operates servers. Google's data-centre locations: https://datacenters.google/locations/

Items: your IP address, device and app information, ad interaction data, diagnostic data, identifiers the SDK creates for this app, and the app set ID, as described above. For the consent check, Google receives your IP address, which it uses to work out your region, and app and device information.

When and how: at launch for the consent check (Free users only) and each time an ad is requested, shown or measured, over encrypted internet connections.

Purpose: serving ads, limiting how often an ad is shown, preventing fraud and abuse and measuring ads, and, for the consent check, finding out whether a consent message is needed and applying your choice. Google also uses such data for its own purposes, which it describes here: https://policies.google.com/technologies/partner-sites

Retention: Google keeps the data for the periods set in its policies; DoseWeek cannot shorten them.

How to refuse: where Google's consent message applies, you can make or change your choice at any time in Settings > Privacy choices for ads. If your choice does not allow ad processing, DoseWeek requests no ads and every Free feature keeps working; the consent check at launch still contacts Google. Where no consent message applies, for example in Korea, Google's consent service offers no way to refuse and DoseWeek does not offer one either, so the only way to use DoseWeek without this ad processing is Plus: once Plus is confirmed, the app requests no ads and makes no consent check.

sections.title: 7. Retention and deletion
paragraphs:
The encrypted server copy is kept while Plus is active. It is deleted 30 days after the end of the last Plus period that the server verified with the App Store or Google Play. Before deleting, the server checks with the store again and keeps the copy if Plus was renewed. If the store cannot be reached, deletion may be postponed by up to 7 days. At any time you can delete only the server copy (reset sync), which keeps your account and the records on your devices, or delete the whole account. If you request direct deletion or withdraw consent, the 30-day waiting period and store-outage extension do not apply. Access stops immediately and the data covered by the request is erased from live storage without delay. Deleting only the server copy keeps the account. Completion is reported after the actual result is confirmed. Server backups are kept for at most 7 days, so deleted data leaves those backups within 7 days. Records on your devices and files you exported or stored separately, for example in a cloud storage service, must be deleted separately. Deleting the DoseWeek account does not cancel a store subscription. DoseWeek account and server-data deletion is reported separately from provider disconnection. If disconnection cannot be confirmed, you receive instructions for manual removal; no automatic retry is promised. After account deletion, the server keeps only a keyed marker of each purchase that was linked to the account, without any link to the account, so that the purchase cannot silently move to another account. This marker is kept for 5 years as a record of payment and supply under Article 6 of the Enforcement Decree of the Korean Act on the Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce, and is then deleted. Records of consumer complaints and dispute handling, such as support requests, are kept for 3 years under the same article. If you bought Plus on Google Play, the separate purchase-verification server keeps its purchase records (a one-way hash of the purchase token, the product, subscription state and times) until 90 days after the latest of the paid-period end, grace-period end and last check, and notification identifiers for 30 days; these records are not linked to a DoseWeek account and are deleted on that schedule. These purchase-verification records hold only the verification state, with no price, payment method or order details, so they are not payment records. Payment records are kept by the store that sold the subscription.

Email wonyoung@wonyoungchoi.dev to request deletion of your DoseWeek account and associated server data without reinstalling the app or subscribing to Plus. Identify the sign-in provider and, if known, your DoseWeek account ID. We explain identity verification by email. Do not send passwords, recovery codes, health records or purchase tokens. Composing or sending the email does not confirm deletion. Account/server-data erasure and provider disconnection outcomes are confirmed and communicated separately. If disconnection cannot be confirmed, we explain manual removal in the provider’s account settings. Canceling a subscription is not a condition of this request; manage store billing separately.

Backup files and CSV export files saved outside the app are not deleted automatically when app data is deleted or the app is uninstalled. Delete them separately through Android's file app or their document provider when needed.
If you used Google Drive backup, delete those copies from the backup list inside the app, or by removing the app's data from your Google account. Uninstalling DoseWeek does not remove them.

You can delete local app data and Drive backups separately. Backups and exports saved with another provider follow that provider's controls. Uninstalling DoseWeek or disconnecting Drive does not itself request deletion of Drive backups or Google food-label SDK diagnostic and usage metrics. Google's processing and retention of those metrics follow Google's terms; DoseWeek cannot directly delete them or state Google's retention period.

If you refuse either optional consent, analytics stays off and core functions remain available. You can withdraw either consent in Settings. Withdrawal stops future analytics collection but does not automatically delete records already sent to Google.

Withdrawing analytics consent stops future collection and requests a reset of local analytics data and its identifier when the SDK is already initialized. If data-deletion recovery occurs before the SDK is initialized, a local reset is requested first when you later consent again to analytics and overseas transfer and activate the SDK. This is not confirmation of Google server deletion or completed disk cleanup.

While analytics is on, the app can show you an analytics deletion request code: open Settings > Usage analytics (optional), open “Analytics deletion request code” and tap “View deletion request code”. If Settings shows a list of sections, as on some wide screens, select “Data management” first. This code contains the app-instance identifier used to locate analytics records for the current installation. If you wish, copy it before turning analytics off or deleting app data and request deletion at wonyoung@wonyoungchoi.dev. Viewing or copying the code does not send a deletion request. Do not send health records.

The code can be shown only while analytics is on. After you turn analytics off or delete app data, that code can no longer be shown or recovered. Without the previous identifier, we may be unable to locate records already sent for that installation. You can still withdraw analytics consent at any time.

Destruction procedure and method: when you delete your account in the app (Settings > Account > Delete account, confirmed with your Apple or Google sign-in), the server deletes in the same request your sign-in links and sessions, the purchase links of the account, your AI record assistant consent record and usage counts, the account record, and the file that holds your encrypted sync copy. Deleting only the server copy (reset sync) deletes that encrypted file and keeps the account. Without a request, the server checks every hour and deletes the encrypted copy 30 days after the last store-confirmed Plus period, as described above. These records exist only in electronic form: the entry is removed from the server’s data file, which is then rewritten, and the encrypted copy file is deleted from the server’s storage. Encrypted server backups are deleted automatically within 7 days of their creation, so a deleted account disappears from the backups within that time. Web server access logs are deleted after at most 11 days, and requests to the account, sync and AI functions are not written to an access log. Records that a law requires us to keep are kept only for the stated period (the purchase marker described above, which has no link to your account, for 5 years, and correspondence about complaints or disputes for 3 years) and are deleted when that period ends.

sections.title: 8. Security
paragraphs: If you turn it on separately, DoseWeek encrypts all your records on the device (injection plans and their changes, dose records, meals, body measurements, supplies and import history) together with supported settings, for automatic backup and sync across both platforms. The settings that sync are appearance (colour and light or dark mode), the weight-change unit, the body map view, whether injection reminders are on, whether reminders show details or the medication name, recording without a plan, supply tracking, and your food search market and search-language choices. When one of these is changed on another device, this device applies it and tells you once about an important change, such as reminders or supply tracking. Sync never turns on an AI feature: you turn it on yourself on each device. Permissions, connections and display choices that belong to a single device are not synced: notification permission, the app lock, health-data, calendar and cloud-storage connections, and widget appearance. When you restore from Settings, the saved settings are applied and the app tells you which settings changed. This is end-to-end encryption: the server keeps only encrypted snapshots and the account and purchase records it needs. Your data key is stored only in a form locked by your recovery code, and the recovery code stays on your devices, so the operator cannot read your health records. The server handles account and provider identifiers, verified Plus state, ciphertext, versions and minimal access metadata, but receives neither readable health records nor your recovery code. A new device needs the recovery code; if it is lost, the developer cannot recover the encrypted data. An empty device may restore after code confirmation; a device with existing records requires a preview and merge confirmation. To recheck subscription status with the store, the server also keeps keyed purchase digests and encrypted lookup references containing an Apple original transaction ID or store purchase token. References use AES-256-GCM with a server-only key separate from the end-to-end health-record keys and are used only for store checks. Account deletion erases references; expired references are pruned after 30 days. Keyed digest markers that prevent duplicate purchase linking are kept for 5 years as records of payment and supply under Article 6 of the Enforcement Decree of the Korean Act on the Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce, and are then deleted. Content you consent to and send to the AI record assistant (Pro) is the exception to end-to-end encryption: the DoseWeek server and Google can read it while an answer is being made. Google can also read it for as long as Google holds it: in memory for up to 24 hours, or for up to 90 days when Google’s abuse checks flag a request, which authorized Google staff may then review.

The optional app lock relies on your device's own screen lock or biometrics through Android's system prompt; DoseWeek stores no biometric data and hides its content in the app switcher while the lock is on. Optional reminders are scheduled only on the device: by default their text reveals nothing about your treatment, the medication name appears only if you enable it, dose amounts never appear, and tapping a reminder only opens the app.

The home-screen widget shows a schedule date, status and day count. Other people who can see your unlocked home screen may see this information. Enabling App Lock hides the schedule in the widget. A medication name appears only when you enable both reminder details and medication-name display; dose amounts never appear. The widget is read-only: tapping it only opens the app and never records an administration. Widget processing stays on the device and makes no separate network transmissions.
When cloud backup is on, this device's copy of the recovery code is sealed with a non-exportable key held in the Android hardware keystore, and transport is TLS to Google's API hosts only.

sections.title: 10. Features added in DoseWeek 1.0.0 (versionCode 12)
paragraphs: This section describes how the features added in DoseWeek 1.0.0 (versionCode 12) for Android handle your data. The optional calendar sync and backup wording in sections 3 and 4 describes the same version. Effective date: September 23, 2026.

Meal records: the meal name, date, optional time and meal kind you enter, and the energy, protein, carbohydrate and fat totals you know, are kept in app-private storage. A value you leave blank stays unknown and is not calculated. Meal records are included in the encrypted backup, can be written to a separate plaintext CSV file only when you ask for it, and are not part of the visit summary. The developer receives no meal information in readable form; if you turn on account sync, meal records are sent to the server only end-to-end encrypted, so the developer cannot read them. Content you consent to and send to the AI record assistant (Pro) is the exception to end-to-end encryption: the DoseWeek server and Google can read it while an answer is being made. Google can also read it for as long as Google holds it: in memory for up to 24 hours, or for up to 90 days when Google’s abuse checks flag a request, which authorized Google staff may then review.

Schedules and body charts: a plan can store a list of injection dates you choose instead of a repeating interval, and the weekly weight-change and BMI charts can show either a published general reference or a personal target you set. The chosen reference and target value are stored on the device and are included in the encrypted backup. A reference is general population information, not advice about your treatment.

Backup format: the new features raise the format number of the encrypted backup file. Backups written by earlier versions can still be restored, but a backup written by the new version cannot be restored by an earlier version. Calendar event links and unsaved drafts are not included in a backup. Your choice of reference medication for the estimate is not included in a backup; choose it again after a restore.

Food data tables: this version includes an offline, read-only food table built from public data (USDA FoodData Central, public domain under CC0 1.0 with attribution requested; UK CoFID under the Open Government Licence v3.0; the Japanese MEXT Standard Tables of Food Composition under the MEXT data-use statement and site terms; Korean MFDS data under the data.go.kr grant with no use restriction). Food search runs only on the device: what you type and the results are not sent anywhere, and the table is not downloaded or updated over the network. Your market and search-language choices and the foods you save as favorites from the table are stored on the device and included in the encrypted backup. Values are shown as the source reports them and are general reference information. The app lists each source, licence and attribution. DoseWeek selected and converted these data; no provider created, reviewed or endorsed this adaptation. Attribution: U.S. Department of Agriculture, Agricultural Research Service. FoodData Central: Foundation Foods, April 2026 bulk release. https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/ · PHE (Public Health England) (2021). Composition of foods integrated dataset (CoFID). © Crown copyright 2021. Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0. · 出典：日本食品標準成分表（八訂）増補2023年（文部科学省） 「日本食品標準成分表（八訂）増補2023年」（文部科学省）を基にDoseWeekが編集・加工（文部科学省が作成したものではありません）。 · 출처: 식품의약품안전처, 전국통합식품영양성분정보(음식)표준데이터 (공공데이터포털 data.go.kr, 데이터기준일자 2026-08-28). 일부 항목 원출처: 농촌진흥청 국가표준식품성분표. DoseWeek never provides a dietary prescription or a prescribing decision.

Optional voice input: only after you start it, accept the explanation and grant microphone permission, DoseWeek uses Android on-device speech recognition on supported devices and languages. If local recognition is unavailable, enter text manually; there is no cloud speech fallback. DoseWeek does not save audio. The editable transcript in the review panel is temporary, is excluded from backups and logs, and is cleared when you leave the screen, lock the app or put it in the background. It does not automatically fill or save clinical fields: enter and confirm facts in the manual record form. Keyboard dictation is a separate system feature whose processing may differ; DoseWeek does not promise that it is always local.

Optional food-label recognition: after separate explanation and consent, and only for a photo you select, DoseWeek uses bundled Google ML Kit text and barcode recognition. Photo contents and recognition results are processed on the device and are not sent to Google by ML Kit. However, the SDK sends Google diagnostics and usage data over HTTPS: an installation identifier, device and hardware information, app information, latency, API settings such as image format and resolution, input/output sizes, feature versions, event types and error codes. SDK maintenance contacts and queued diagnostic uploads may occur after the review panel closes. This exception applies only to food-label recognition, not to other AI features or developer analytics. Declining consent preserves manual entry. No recognition starts merely by installing or opening DoseWeek.

medicalDisclaimer.title: Medical disclaimer
medicalDisclaimer.body: DoseWeek is a personal record-keeping tool, not a medical device. It does not diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent disease and does not provide medical advice or dose or timing decisions. Follow the product's prescribing information and guidance from a qualified healthcare professional for medication and treatment decisions. If you think you may be experiencing an emergency, contact your local emergency service immediately. The mg amount remaining is a model-based estimate for reference only. It is not a measured blood concentration and does not predict treatment response, medicine effects, side effects or whether an injection is safe. It is not medical advice. Do not use it to change your dose or injection schedule; discuss treatment decisions with your doctor or pharmacist.

sections.title: Processing purposes, consent and safeguards
paragraphs: DoseWeek processes medication names, schedules and administration records, body measurements, meals and protein, symptoms and notes to keep the records you request. Health records stay on the device by default. Optional account and encrypted sync handling, including identifiers, purchase verification and server retention, is explained in the account/sync disclosure. General account processing relies on providing the requested service; optional health sync requires separate explicit health-data consent. OS permission, agreement to Terms and acknowledgement of this policy do not replace that consent. Analytics and any required overseas-transfer consent remain separate and optional.

Health-platform access is optional and read-only, limited to the metrics listed in the health section. DoseWeek requests no health-platform writing or deletion permission. You can revoke access in device settings and continue manual entry. DoseWeek does not publicly disclose or sell recorded health content, including medication and body-measurement records, share that content for advertising, or use it to select ads. Health content is excluded from analytics events, screen names and logs sent to advertising or analytics services. User-chosen exports, calendars and file providers remain under your control and those recipients' policies.

Access controls, device locks, encrypted backup envelopes, encrypted transport and separate recovery keys protect the data within their stated scope. Encryption does not make account identifiers, IP addresses or health-revealing metadata anonymous. Records are retained for the purposes and periods described in the retention and account/sync sections. After deletion, data is made unavailable and removed without undue delay; encrypted backup copies must be removed within 7 days and must not reappear as active records after restoration.

sections.title: Your rights and regional protections
paragraphs:
The privacy officer is Wonyoung Labs. Request access, correction, erasure, restriction, withdrawal, objection or a machine-readable export through app settings or wonyoung@wonyoungchoi.dev. We verify only what is necessary to confirm your identity. In Korea, access requests receive access or a reasoned decision within 10 days; any lawful deferral is explained. Withdrawal and user-requested deletion do not wait for the subscription-retention period. If a request is refused or limited, we explain the legal reason and how to appeal to this contact. You may also complain to your local supervisory authority; in Korea, PIPC, KISA (118) and the Personal Information Dispute Mediation Committee provide complaint and dispute channels.

DoseWeek is for people aged 18 or older. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 14. If we learn that a child under 14 has created an account or sent us personal information, we delete that account and its server data without delay. A parent or legal guardian can ask for this at wonyoung@wonyoungchoi.dev.

Version 1.0.6 is not offered for sale in the EU/EEA, the UK or Switzerland. We have not appointed an EU or UK representative for this version. This sales exclusion does not remove applicable rights or safeguards for existing users. Where GDPR applies, Art. 6 service necessity or consent covers ordinary data, and Art. 9 explicit consent covers optional health sync. Applicable access, correction, erasure, restriction, objection and machine-readable portability requests are normally answered within 1 month; a lawful extension and its reason are notified within that month.

In Japan, acquisition of special-care-required health information needs prior consent where APPI applies. APPI Art. 28 foreign provision needs informed consent or a qualifying equivalent-protection route. In Brazil, LGPD health-data consent is specific and highlighted; access, correction, deletion, withdrawal and other applicable rights are available through the same contact, including in Portuguese. Ordinary legitimate interest is not used as the health-data basis.

International safeguards must be verified for each recipient and onward route. Korea adequacy does not authorize every onward transfer. Where applicable, EU adequacy or verified DPF coverage, SCC and supplementary measures, UK adequacy or IDTA/Addendum, and Brazil ANPD-compliant mechanisms must be recorded separately. EU SCC do not automatically satisfy ANPD requirements.

sections.title: Data incidents and breach response
paragraphs: Report a suspected privacy incident to wonyoung@wonyoungchoi.dev without sending health records, passwords or recovery codes. We assess intrusions and unauthorized SDK disclosures, contain exposure, preserve evidence and identify affected data and recipients. Encryption is assessed together with key protection and account or health-revealing metadata; it is not an automatic exemption.

In Korea, affected individuals are notified without undue delay and normally within 72 hours of learning of a leak, with any permitted exception documented. PIPA reporting to PIPC or KISA is due within 72 hours where at least 1,000 people are affected, sensitive or unique-identification data is involved, or qualifying external unauthorized access caused the leak. These triggers are independent; a small health-data incident can still require reporting.

Where the FTC Health Breach Notification Rule applies, individuals are notified without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery. For 500 or more affected people, the FTC is notified at the same time as individuals; for fewer than 500, within 60 calendar days after the end of the calendar year. If 500 or more affected residents are in one state or jurisdiction, required media notice is also given. Required electronic and substitute notices follow the Rule. Where GDPR applies, qualifying authority notice is within 72 hours of awareness unless risk is unlikely, and high-risk individuals are informed without undue delay.

sections.title: AI record assistant (Pro)
paragraphs:
This part applies from the first DoseWeek version that has the AI record assistant (1.0.6). Until that version is released, the app has no AI record assistant and sends nothing to Google for it.

Purpose: to create the weekly summaries, general meal ideas and app-help answers you ask for. The AI record assistant is an optional feature included in the Pro subscription. Answers come from AI, not a person, and it does not give medical advice.

Data processed: the records and meal choices you confirm on screen before sending, and app-help questions and current conversation history. The records are dose counts (on time, late, skipped), the change in the weight you entered yourself, how many times you logged each kind of symptom, the number of days with a meal log together with your protein average and goal, and your streak in weeks. For meal ideas we also send the meal kind, preferences, allergies and disliked foods you choose. Your language and region setting is also sent. Only app help sends the questions you type and the current conversation history, along with the app version, the platform and the current screen. Model requests built from records exclude medication names and doses, notes, recorded food names, photos, dates, names, email addresses and account identifiers. Meal kinds, preferences, allergies and disliked foods are sent only as values chosen from predefined lists. App help also sends your question and current conversation history, so do not enter names, contact details or other people’s health information. DoseWeek separately processes account and connection information needed for sign-in, usage counts and consent management. Information read from Health Connect is not used for AI features either and is not sent to the AI record assistant.

Legal basis: health information is sensitive, so we process it only with a consent that is separate from every other consent. In Korea this is the consent under Article 23 of the Personal Information Protection Act. We ask when you first turn the feature on, and each time records are sent we show what will be sent and ask you to confirm again.

Retention: The DoseWeek server does not keep what you send or the answers. Google does not use what you send or the answers to train AI models. To speed up responses, Google may hold this content in memory for up to 24 hours, and if Google’s automated abuse checks flag a request, Google may store that request for up to 90 days, and authorized Google staff may review it. DoseWeek does not save your conversations. Weekly summary cards are saved only on your device, at most 2, and are left out of sync and every backup. Usage counts (without content) are kept for up to 2 months, and consent records for as long as the account exists. If you report an answer and choose “Include the answer text”, only that answer is kept for 30 days.

Processor: DoseWeek entrusts the creation of AI answers to Google. Gemini, an AI model from Google, runs on Google Cloud Vertex AI, a platform Google now calls Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. DoseWeek uses Google’s Global location (the global endpoint). Google states that such requests “may be processed in any Google Cloud location around the world”. The country where this content is processed can change with each request, depending on which Google servers handle it; Google decides this, so the country cannot be fixed or named in advance. Recipient: Google Cloud Korea LLC (the contracting entity Google’s terms name for a billing address in the Republic of Korea; Seoul, Republic of Korea) and Google Asia Pacific Pte. Ltd. with its affiliates, including Google LLC (United States) (contact: https://support.google.com/cloud/contact/dpo). Google acts as a processor under Google’s Cloud Data Processing Addendum.

Where it is processed and how it travels: To create AI answers, DoseWeek sends what you confirm to Google and entrusts Google with processing it. This transfers your information to another country. Country: Global (no single country). DoseWeek uses Google’s Global location (the global endpoint), and Google states that such requests “may be processed in any Google Cloud location around the world”. The country where this content is processed can change with each request, depending on which Google servers handle it; Google decides this, so the country cannot be fixed or named in advance. Google lists its locations at https://cloud.google.com/about/locations. Of the recipients named in this notice, Google LLC is located in the United States and Google Asia Pacific Pte. Ltd. in Singapore; the data-protection systems of these two countries are described next. The United States has no comprehensive federal law on personal information; sector-specific federal laws and state laws apply, and it takes part in the APEC Cross-Border Privacy Rules (CBPR) system. Google Asia Pacific Pte. Ltd. is located in Singapore. Singapore has a comprehensive personal data protection law (the Personal Data Protection Act 2012) and takes part in the APEC CBPR system. The app encrypts the content once more to the DoseWeek server’s public key, so Cloudflare, which relays the request, sees only ciphertext. The overseas transfer of connection information that Cloudflare handles, such as your IP address, follows the overseas-transfer notice in this policy.
AI training and advertising: we do not use the records and questions you send for AI training or advertising, and we do not sell them.

How this differs from end-to-end encryption: while an answer is being made, the DoseWeek server and Google can read what you sent to the AI record assistant. Google can also read it for as long as Google holds it: in memory for up to 24 hours, or for up to 90 days when Google’s abuse checks flag a request, which authorized Google staff may then review. End-to-end encryption applies only to sync and backup data.
Automated decisions: AI answers are for reference. The AI makes no decision that affects your rights or obligations.

Withdrawing consent and deleting: in Settings > AI record assistant you can withdraw consent and delete saved AI summaries at any time. After you withdraw, no records are sent to the AI. Deleting your account also deletes your usage counts and consent records. If you do not consent, the other Pro and Plus features keep working.
Age: the AI record assistant is only for people aged 18 or older. You confirm your age yourself; we do not ask for a date of birth.

AI labels and safety messages: every AI answer carries a label saying it was made by AI and is not medical advice, and each answer has a Report button. When content is detected as requesting medical advice, such as dosing, diagnosis or medication guidance, the app shows a fixed safety message instead of generating an AI answer. Detection can miss or misclassify requests, so do not use the feature to make health decisions. If a message looks like an emergency or a crisis, the app shows the numbers for your store region: 119 and 109 in Korea, 119 and the Yorisoi Hotline (0120-279-338) in Japan, 911 and 988 in the United States. Elsewhere it points to your local emergency number and findahelpline.com.

support.title: Help for DoseWeek on Android
support.intro:
This text takes effect on October 3, 2026. The parts about accounts, sync, Plus, ads and other new features describe the first DoseWeek version that has them (1.0.6) and apply from the release of that version. Earlier versions do not have these features.

You may optionally sign in to a DoseWeek account with Apple or Google. Existing local-record features remain available without sign-in. Linking a verified Plus subscription from either store to the same DoseWeek account enables encrypted sync on both platforms. Verified Plus also shares ad removal and Plus tools across both platforms. To revoke Apple sign-in, the server may retain an Apple refresh token encrypted with a separate server key, distinct from health-record end-to-end keys.

Usage analytics and its international transfer each need separate optional consent, independent of account sign-in, sync and ad choices. Refusing either keeps analytics off and core features available. Health records and recovery codes are not sent to analytics.
support.privacyWarning: Do not include health information, medication or administration records, personal notes, a backup file, or a recovery code in a support email.

steps.title: Open DoseWeek and set it up
steps.body: Confirm that you are 18 or older, read the privacy notice and choose whether to allow optional usage analytics; every core feature works without it. Then set up your plan, or restore a backup, import records from another app or manage records without a plan.

steps.title: Set your schedule
steps.body: Choose your medication and dose, then pick Repeating schedule or Pick dates; you can change the plan later in Settings > Treatment plan. Reminders are optional.

steps.title: Record an injection
steps.body: On Today, tap Record administration, answer Yes, I did, then check the details and save. Your records appear in History, where you can also add a past injection or correct a record.

steps.title: Record meals
steps.body: In the Body tab, open Meals. Enter only the values you know, or search the built-in offline food list.

steps.title: Import earlier records
steps.body: Tap Import records from another app at the top of History or Settings. Review the records from your CSV, TSV or JSON file; only the ones you select are added.

steps.title: Backups, reminders and privacy choices
steps.body:
In Settings, export an encrypted backup, adjust Notifications and change Usage analytics (optional) at any time. Add the DoseWeek widget to your Home Screen to see your next injection at a glance.

While Plus is active, you can separately consent to turn on automatic server backup and sync. App records are end-to-end encrypted on the device; the server cannot read the backed-up contents. Free users can still manually export and import files and use the in-app backup reminder.

Android OS Google Drive Auto Backup includes DoseWeek app data only while Plus is verified and active; it then backs up the database, keys and records together as one complete set. If Plus is not active or cannot be verified, for example offline or when the store check fails, DoseWeek skips that backup run instead of sending an empty or partial backup, so the previous backup stays as it is. DoseWeek does not delete existing Drive backups, and you can still restore an existing backup. This backup is kept in your Google account under Google's rules, separately from DoseWeek server copies; you can manage or delete it in your Google account's backup settings. Users of 1.0.5 receive a one-time notice explaining this change and how to export a file. The notice does not block use of the app.

answers:

faq.question: Do I need to sign in or create an account?
answers:
This text takes effect on October 3, 2026. The parts about accounts, sync, Plus, ads and other new features describe the first DoseWeek version that has them (1.0.6) and apply from the release of that version. Earlier versions do not have these features.

You may optionally sign in to a DoseWeek account with Apple or Google. Existing local-record features remain available without sign-in. Verified Plus also shares ad removal and Plus tools across both platforms. If you turn it on separately, DoseWeek encrypts all your records on the device (injection plans and their changes, dose records, meals, body measurements, supplies and import history) together with supported settings, for automatic backup and sync across both platforms. The settings that sync are appearance (colour and light or dark mode), the weight-change unit, the body map view, whether injection reminders are on, whether reminders show details or the medication name, recording without a plan, supply tracking, and your food search market and search-language choices. When one of these is changed on another device, this device applies it and tells you once about an important change, such as reminders or supply tracking. When you restore from Settings, the saved settings are applied and the app tells you which settings changed. A new device needs the recovery code; if it is lost, the developer cannot recover the encrypted data. An empty device may restore after code confirmation; a device with existing records requires a preview and merge confirmation. To recheck subscription status with the store, the server also keeps keyed purchase digests and encrypted lookup references containing an Apple original transaction ID or store purchase token. References use AES-256-GCM with a server-only key separate from the end-to-end health-record keys and are used only for store checks. Account deletion erases references; expired references are pruned after 30 days. Keyed digest markers that prevent duplicate purchase linking are kept for 5 years as records of payment and supply under Article 6 of the Enforcement Decree of the Korean Act on the Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce, and are then deleted. A public announcement can be checked when the app opens, before onboarding. The per-announcement ‘Do not show for one week’ choice stays on this device. The announcement request may process connection data such as an IP address; the web server keeps an access log of the IP address, time, requested address, response status and size, referrer and browser or app identifier (user agent) for up to 11 days. This request also passes through Cloudflare; the privacy policy gives the overseas transfer details.

faq.question: Does DoseWeek use AI or Health Connect?
answers:
This part applies from the first DoseWeek version that has the AI record assistant (1.0.6). Until that version is released, the app has no AI record assistant and sends nothing to Google for it.

DoseWeek 1.0.6 for Android includes the optional AI record assistant (Pro). It is processed on a server, not on the device. Only after separate consent, generative AI on Google Cloud Vertex AI (Global, no fixed country) creates weekly summaries, general meal ideas and app-help answers. No other feature uses generative AI. Optional on-device voice and food-label recognition help with input; Google food-label SDK diagnostics require separate consent, as described in the Privacy Policy. Health Connect is now an optional read-only import of weight, height, body fat percentage, and lean body mass: the app asks for read permissions only, never write or delete, and imports nothing until you grant that permission. Every administration record is still entered and confirmed by hand.

faq.question: Does DoseWeek provide notifications, reminders, or widgets?
answers: Optional reminders and a home-screen widget are available. DoseWeek 1.0.6 can schedule local reminders on your device for the next dose, a follow-up after a missed dose, and low supply. They stay off until you turn them on and grant the notification permission. By default the reminder text reveals nothing about your treatment; the medication name appears only if you enable it, and dose amounts never appear. Tapping a reminder only opens the app, so nothing is ever recorded from a notification. There are no wearable apps.

faq.question: Can I back up or restore my records?

The file-backup details below describe manual export and import. Plus automatic server backup is a separate path.

Yes. In Settings, use Android's system file picker to manually save all app data in an AES-256-GCM encrypted file, and select that file to restore. A separate high-entropy recovery code is required. Backups can be restored only in DoseWeek for Android. DoseWeek on other platforms uses a different backup format, so backups cannot be moved between platforms.

This export needs no DoseWeek account and no broad storage permission, and the export itself uses no network access. If you choose an external or cloud document provider, its terms and policies apply. In either case the developer receives neither the file nor its recovery code and cannot reset a lost code or decrypt the file. Restore completely validates the file before replacing current data in one atomic local transaction.

faq.question: How do I delete all records?
answers:
Use Delete all data in DoseWeek Settings. Uninstalling the app also causes Android to delete local app data. Backup files saved outside the app are not deleted automatically; delete them separately through Android's file app or their document provider. Backups you uploaded to your own Google Drive are not removed by uninstalling either: delete them from the backup list inside the app, or by removing the app's data from your Google account.

The encrypted server copy is kept while Plus is active. It is deleted 30 days after the end of the last Plus period that the server verified with the App Store or Google Play. Before deleting, the server checks with the store again and keeps the copy if Plus was renewed. If the store cannot be reached, deletion may be postponed by up to 7 days. At any time you can delete only the server copy (reset sync), which keeps your account and the records on your devices, or delete the whole account. If you request direct deletion or withdraw consent, the 30-day waiting period and store-outage extension do not apply. Access stops immediately and the data covered by the request is erased from live storage without delay. Deleting only the server copy keeps the account. Completion is reported after the actual result is confirmed. Server backups are kept for at most 7 days, so deleted data leaves those backups within 7 days. Records on your devices and files you exported or stored separately, for example in a cloud storage service, must be deleted separately. Deleting the DoseWeek account does not cancel a store subscription. DoseWeek account and server-data deletion is reported separately from provider disconnection. If disconnection cannot be confirmed, you receive instructions for manual removal; no automatic retry is promised. After account deletion, the server keeps only a keyed marker of each purchase that was linked to the account, without any link to the account, so that the purchase cannot silently move to another account. This marker is kept for 5 years as a record of payment and supply under Article 6 of the Enforcement Decree of the Korean Act on the Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce, and is then deleted. Records of consumer complaints and dispute handling, such as support requests, are kept for 3 years under the same article. If you bought Plus on Google Play, the separate purchase-verification server keeps its purchase records (a one-way hash of the purchase token, the product, subscription state and times) until 90 days after the latest of the paid-period end, grace-period end and last check, and notification identifiers for 30 days; these records are not linked to a DoseWeek account and are deleted on that schedule. These purchase-verification records hold only the verification state, with no price, payment method or order details, so they are not payment records. Payment records are kept by the store that sold the subscription.

Email wonyoung@wonyoungchoi.dev to request deletion of your DoseWeek account and associated server data without reinstalling the app or subscribing to Plus. Identify the sign-in provider and, if known, your DoseWeek account ID. We explain identity verification by email. Do not send passwords, recovery codes, health records or purchase tokens. Composing or sending the email does not confirm deletion. Account/server-data erasure and provider disconnection outcomes are confirmed and communicated separately. If disconnection cannot be confirmed, we explain manual removal in the provider’s account settings. Canceling a subscription is not a condition of this request; manage store billing separately.

faq.question: Choose dates and times
answers: Available in DoseWeek Android 1.0.0 (versionCode 12) and later.

Tap a date or time to open the system picker. Use the month or year control for older dates, and AM/PM when shown. Cancel keeps your entry; confirming changes the draft. Save the record to keep your changes. Use the pencil to type dates as YYYY-MM-DD or YYYYMMDD and 24-hour times as HH:mm or HHmm.

faq.question: Correct a record
answers: Available in DoseWeek Android 1.0.0 (versionCode 12) and later.

In History, choose the date, then Edit on the record. Save to update that same record. If you change its date, the updated record is under the new date. Imported Health Connect measurements are read-only: correct them in the original app.

faq.question: Add a past injection
answers: Available in DoseWeek Android 1.0.0 (versionCode 12) and later.

In History, choose a past date and add a past administration. Confirm the medicine, dose, unit, and actual time before saving. You can manage records without creating a plan. Records without a plan do not change schedules or stock. For records linked to a plan, check whether stock will be deducted. Restoring an encrypted backup replaces data; it is a separate action. Stock deduction for past entries starts off; review the displayed choice. If a linked plan’s latest injection changes, future unresolved dates may be adjusted.

faq.question: Find missing measurements
answers: Available in DoseWeek Android 1.0.0 (versionCode 12) and later.

First check the original app and Health Connect. In DoseWeek’s Body screen, check the metric and period. In Settings, open Health Connect and choose Import now. For missing results, check read permissions and permission for past records separately from syncing in the original app. The measurement date is when it was measured, not when DoseWeek imported it.

faq.question: Understand left and right
answers: Available in DoseWeek Android 1.0.0 (versionCode 12) and later.

Left and right always mean your own body. My body and Front view change only how the diagram is displayed. Your selection and saved records keep the same body side. Check the selected name or open the site list to choose by text. You can change the view in Settings too.
Upper-left abdomen · Upper-right abdomen · Lower-left abdomen · Lower-right abdomen · Left thigh · Right thigh · Left upper arm · Right upper arm

faq.question: Can I record meals and nutrition?
answers: Available in DoseWeek Android 1.0.0 (versionCode 12) and later.

In the Body tab, the Meals section takes what you type. Enter the food name and the totals you know (energy, protein, carbohydrate, fat) and leave anything you do not know blank; a blank value stays unknown. A meal holds up to 100 items and you can keep up to 1,000 favorites. You can also search the built-in food list offline. You can now search for 200 foods in the list using names in 17 languages. Search starts with all supported languages; choose specific languages in Settings if you prefer. Records stay on the device and travel in the encrypted backup. Meal records are not nutrition advice or a prescription.

faq.question: Can I choose specific injection dates?
answers: Available in DoseWeek Android 1.0.0 (versionCode 12) and later.

In the schedule editor, choose the chosen-dates mode and pick several dates in the calendar. The selection is shown as a preview, and a future date closer than the minimum interval in the verified medicine information is blocked at save. Records you already made in the past are never blocked. After the last chosen date the plan stays active and asks you to add more dates.

faq.question: What do the reference ranges on charts mean?
answers: Available in DoseWeek Android 1.0.0 (versionCode 12) and later.

On the weekly weight-change and BMI charts you can show a published general reference (WHO, CDC, NHS, NICE, the Korean Society for the Study of Obesity, the Japan Society for the Study of Obesity) or a personal target you set. Nothing is preselected, and the label shows only the range and its source, never a category word. A reference is general population information, not advice about your treatment, and your clinician may set a different target.

faq.question: How does calendar sync work?
answers: Available in DoseWeek Android 1.0.0 (versionCode 12) and later.

It stays off until you turn it on in Settings, and asks for calendar permission separately at that point. Once on, it writes up to 24 upcoming injection days within the next 84 days as 30-minute events in the one calendar you choose. The title is “Personal reminder” by default and becomes “Injection day” only if you choose it; medication, dose, site, notes and alerts are never written. The app updates or deletes only the events it created, and leaves alone any event you edited yourself. Turning sync off lets you delete upcoming events, and events left in the calendar stay there after you uninstall the app.

faq.question: Can an older version restore a new backup?
answers: This applies to DoseWeek Android 1.0.0 (versionCode 12) and later.

No. The new features raise the backup format number, so an earlier version refuses a file written by the new one. The opposite direction still works: backups written by earlier versions restore in the new version. Meal records and chart reference settings are included in the backup; calendar event links and unsaved drafts are not. Your choice of reference medication for the estimate is not included in a backup; choose it again after a restore.

faq.question: Which devices and Android versions are supported?
answers: This applies to DoseWeek Android versionCode 13 and later.

Use DoseWeek on Android 14 or later. On Android 8.0 to Android 13, you can keep using the version already installed (versionCode 12), but it will not receive updates, and Google Play will not offer new installs on those devices. Some optional AI features need a compatible device; you can still enter records yourself if they are unavailable.

faq.question: Can I bring records from another app?
answers: Available in DoseWeek Android 1.0.0 (versionCode 12) and later.

You can import past administrations from a CSV, TSV or JSON file, or paste a table directly. One import takes up to 10,000 rows and the saved review draft is limited to 1 MiB. Symptom and unclassified rows cannot be saved yet and must be deselected. Rows that may be duplicates are marked for review, and nothing is saved until you confirm. This is not a backup restore; the preparation guide is at doseweek-legal.wonyoungchoi.dev/import/.

faq.question: Is DoseWeek free?
answers: Yes. DoseWeek is a free download on Google Play, and Free users see ads. Recording, History, Body charts, the fixed 4, 8 and 12-week visit summary, meals, manual file exports and imports, backup reminders, calendar sync, reminders, the widget and the app lock remain free.
Plus is an optional auto-renewing subscription, monthly or annual, that removes ads and adds extra tools. The price and billing period are shown in the app and on Google Play before you buy.

faq.question: What does Plus add, and what stays free?
answers:
Plus removes ads and adds four tools: period summaries that compare a week or month with the one before; a visit summary editor for the period (up to 26 weeks or a custom range of up to 365 days), sections, order, layout, paper size and whether the records table is included; Today layout presets for the order and visibility of Today's extra cards; and meal templates that open as an unsaved draft for you to review. The tools use only values you recorded and give no medical advice.

You may optionally sign in to a DoseWeek account with Apple or Google. Existing local-record features remain available without sign-in. Linking a verified Plus subscription from either store to the same DoseWeek account enables encrypted sync on both platforms. Verified Plus also shares ad removal and Plus tools across both platforms. To revoke Apple sign-in, the server may retain an Apple refresh token encrypted with a separate server key, distinct from health-record end-to-end keys.

While Plus is active, you can separately consent to turn on automatic server backup and sync. App records are end-to-end encrypted on the device; the server cannot read the backed-up contents. Free users can still manually export and import files and use the in-app backup reminder.

Android OS Google Drive Auto Backup includes DoseWeek app data only while Plus is verified and active; it then backs up the database, keys and records together as one complete set. If Plus is not active or cannot be verified, for example offline or when the store check fails, DoseWeek skips that backup run instead of sending an empty or partial backup, so the previous backup stays as it is. DoseWeek does not delete existing Drive backups, and you can still restore an existing backup. This backup is kept in your Google account under Google's rules, separately from DoseWeek server copies; you can manage or delete it in your Google account's backup settings. Users of 1.0.5 receive a one-time notice explaining this change and how to export a file. The notice does not block use of the app.

If you turn it on separately, DoseWeek encrypts all your records on the device (injection plans and their changes, dose records, meals, body measurements, supplies and import history) together with supported settings, for automatic backup and sync across both platforms. The settings that sync are appearance (colour and light or dark mode), the weight-change unit, the body map view, whether injection reminders are on, whether reminders show details or the medication name, recording without a plan, supply tracking, and your food search market and search-language choices. When one of these is changed on another device, this device applies it and tells you once about an important change, such as reminders or supply tracking. Sync never turns on an AI feature: you turn it on yourself on each device. Permissions, connections and display choices that belong to a single device are not synced: notification permission, the app lock, health-data, calendar and cloud-storage connections, and widget appearance. When you restore from Settings, the saved settings are applied and the app tells you which settings changed. This is end-to-end encryption: the server keeps only encrypted snapshots and the account and purchase records it needs. Your data key is stored only in a form locked by your recovery code, and the recovery code stays on your devices, so the operator cannot read your health records. The server handles account and provider identifiers, verified Plus state, ciphertext, versions and minimal access metadata, but receives neither readable health records nor your recovery code. A new device needs the recovery code; if it is lost, the developer cannot recover the encrypted data. An empty device may restore after code confirmation; a device with existing records requires a preview and merge confirmation. To recheck subscription status with the store, the server also keeps keyed purchase digests and encrypted lookup references containing an Apple original transaction ID or store purchase token. References use AES-256-GCM with a server-only key separate from the end-to-end health-record keys and are used only for store checks. Account deletion erases references; expired references are pruned after 30 days. Keyed digest markers that prevent duplicate purchase linking are kept for 5 years as records of payment and supply under Article 6 of the Enforcement Decree of the Korean Act on the Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce, and are then deleted. Content you consent to and send to the AI record assistant (Pro) is the exception to end-to-end encryption: the DoseWeek server and Google can read it while an answer is being made. Google can also read it for as long as Google holds it: in memory for up to 24 hours, or for up to 90 days when Google’s abuse checks flag a request, which authorized Google staff may then review.

Recording, History, Body charts, the fixed 4, 8 and 12-week visit summary, meals, manual file exports and imports, backup reminders, calendar sync, reminders, the widget and the app lock remain free. If Plus ends, your records, templates and saved settings are kept, and you can still view and delete them; visit summary settings and the Today layout return to the Free defaults until Plus is back.

faq.question: How do I cancel or change my plan?
answers: Plus renews automatically until you cancel. Cancel in Google Play under Payments & subscriptions > Subscriptions, which you can open from Settings in DoseWeek. Cancel before the renewal date to avoid the next charge; Plus stays on until the end of the period you paid for.

Switching from monthly to annual takes effect immediately, and Google Play credits the unused monthly time toward the annual plan; switching from annual to monthly takes effect at your next renewal date. Refunds are handled by Google Play under its policies. Uninstalling the app or deleting its data does not cancel the subscription.

faq.question: How do I restore Plus on a new device or after reinstalling?

faq.question: Why do I see ads, and how do I change my ad choices?
answers: Ads keep the free version free. Free users see a banner on History and in the Measurements section of Body, and occasionally a full-screen ad after closing certain help or food-settings sheets; ads never appear on Today, in the record flow or on safety notices. Ads are non-personalized, and Plus removes them. You can also choose to watch one ad to use DoseWeek without ads for 24 hours; it is optional and not a purchase, and closing the ad early grants nothing. You can earn at most two rewards in any rolling 24 hours, and remaining ad-free time never exceeds 48 hours. While a pass is active, another rewarded ad is offered only when 24 hours or less remain. The pass pauses if the device clock is set back more than five minutes from the latest time the app has seen. While the pass is active, automatic ads and Plus subscription offers are hidden.

Open Settings > Privacy choices for ads to review or change Google's ad consent where your region requires it; elsewhere it explains that no choice is needed. Ad choices are separate from Usage analytics (optional) and from the 18+ confirmation. If ad processing is not allowed, the app shows no ads and every Free feature keeps working. To report an inappropriate ad, tap the AdChoices icon on the ad or use Report an ad in Settings; do not add health details.

faq.question: I bought DoseWeek when it was a paid app. What changes for me?
answers: New and prior users keep existing core features Free. No separate prior-buyer Plus grant is offered; the prior-buyer claim/code program is retired. An earlier purchase alone starts neither Plus nor a charge. Only the standard free trial applies, for first-time subscribers whose eligibility the store confirms and under the displayed conditions. Applicable statutory rights remain protected. Perpetual ad-free use is not guaranteed. Platform and consumer-law review of historical ad-free rights remains pending.

Recording, History, Body charts, the fixed 4, 8 and 12-week visit summary, meals, manual file exports and imports, backup reminders, calendar sync, reminders, the widget and the app lock remain free. A one-time notice in the app explains the change, and you can read it again in Settings > About > What's new.

contact.title: Contact support
contact.body: Email wonyoung@wonyoungchoi.dev with your Android version, device model, steps that caused the problem, and what you expected. Do not send health information, medication or administration records, personal notes, a backup file, or a recovery code.

emergency.title: Medical questions and emergencies
emergency.body: DoseWeek support does not provide medical advice, diagnosis, treatment, or dose or timing decisions. Ask a qualified healthcare professional about treatment. If you think you may be experiencing an emergency, do not wait for an email response; contact your local emergency service immediately.

AppleまたはGoogleでDoseWeekアカウントに任意でログインできます。ログインしなくても従来の端末内記録機能を使えます。いずれかのストアで確認済みのPlusを同じアカウントに連携すると、両方のプラットフォームで暗号化同期を利用できます。確認済みのPlusなら、広告の非表示とPlusの機能も両方のプラットフォームで利用できます。Appleの連携を解除するため、サーバーはAppleの更新トークンを別のサーバー鍵で暗号化して保管する場合があります。健康記録のエンドツーエンド暗号化鍵とは異なります。

privacy.scope:
この内容は2026年10月3日から適用されます。アカウント、同期、Plus、広告などの新機能に関する部分は、これらの機能を最初に備えるDoseWeekのバージョン(1.0.6)について説明しており、そのバージョンの公開時から適用されます。それより前のバージョンにこれらの機能はありません。

このポリシーはAndroid版DoseWeek 1.0.0 (versionCode 12) 以降に適用されます。現在のバージョンは1.0.5です。

sections.title: 1. 適用範囲と責任者
paragraphs:
DoseWeekアプリと本ポリシーは、大韓民国を拠点とする個人事業Wonyoung Labsが運営しています。データの取り扱いに関する質問はwonyoung@wonyoungchoi.devへお送りください。

Android版DoseWeekは18歳以上の方が利用できます。生年月日や数字で表した年齢の入力を求めたり、それらを送信したりすることはありません。対象バージョンに対する利用資格の選択のみを端末に保存します。利用資格を拒否するか確認しない場合、通常のアプリ機能とAIは利用できません。既存のローカル記録は削除されません。暗号化バックアップファイルと復旧コードのエクスポートのみが利用でき、アプリロックを有効にしている場合は認証が必要です。利用状況の分析、国外移転、AI機能への同意はそれぞれ別です。

AppleまたはGoogleでDoseWeekアカウントに任意でログインできます。ログインしなくても従来の端末内記録機能を使えます。いずれかのストアで確認済みのPlusを同じアカウントに連携すると、両方のプラットフォームで暗号化同期を利用できます。確認済みのPlusなら、広告の非表示とPlusの機能も両方のプラットフォームで利用できます。Appleの連携を解除するため、サーバーはAppleの更新トークンを別のサーバー鍵で暗号化して保管する場合があります。健康記録のエンドツーエンド暗号化鍵とは異なります。

別途有効にすると、すべての記録（注射計画とその変更、投与記録、食事、身体の測定値、在庫、取り込み履歴）と対応する設定を端末上で暗号化し、両プラットフォームの間で自動バックアップと同期を行います。同期する設定は、外観（カラーとライト・ダークモード）、体重変化の単位、ボディマップの表示方法、注射リマインダーのオン・オフ、通知に詳細や薬の名前を表示するかどうか、計画なしで記録だけを行うかどうか、在庫の追跡、食品検索の地域と検索言語の選択です。別の端末でこれらの設定を変更すると、この端末にも適用し、リマインダーや在庫の追跡などの重要な変更は一度お知らせします。同期によってAI機能がオンになることはなく、端末ごとにご自身でオンにします。通知の許可、アプリロック、健康データ・カレンダー・クラウドストレージとの連携、ウィジェットの外観は端末ごとに決める項目で、同期しません。設定から復元すると、保存されていた設定を適用し、どの設定が変わったかをお知らせします。これはエンドツーエンド暗号化です。サーバーに残るのは暗号化されたスナップショットと、必要なアカウント・購入の記録だけです。データ鍵は復旧コードでロックした形でのみ保存され、復旧コードは利用者の端末にだけあるため、運営者も健康記録を読めません。サーバーはアカウントとログイン事業者の識別子、確認済みPlus状態、暗号文、版情報と最小限のアクセス情報を扱いますが、読める健康記録や復旧コードは受け取りません。新しい端末では復旧コードが必要です。紛失すると開発者も復元できません。空の端末はコードの確認後に復元を始められますが、記録のある端末では事前確認と統合の承認が必要です。ストアで購読状態を再確認するため、サーバーは購入識別子の鍵付きダイジェストと、Appleの元の取引IDまたはストア購入トークンを含む暗号化された照会参照も保存します。参照は健康記録のエンドツーエンド暗号化鍵とは別のサーバー専用鍵でAES-256-GCM暗号化し、ストア確認にのみ使用します。アカウント削除時に参照を消去し、期限切れの参照は30日後に削除します。購入の重複連携を防ぐための鍵付きダイジェスト標識は、韓国の「電子商取引等における消費者保護に関する法律施行令」第6条に基づく代金決済および財貨等の供給に関する記録として5年間保管し、その後削除します。AI記録アシスタント（Pro）に同意して送信した内容は、エンドツーエンド暗号化の例外です。この内容は、回答を作成している間、DoseWeekサーバーとGoogleが読み取れます。Googleは、保持している間もこの内容を読み取れます。保持期間はメモリ上で最大24時間、不正利用検知で疑いがあると判定されたリクエストは最大90日間で、その場合は権限のあるGoogleの担当者が確認することがあります。

健康情報の同期には、一般のアカウント情報の処理、利用規約、利用分析とは別の任意の同意が必要です。OSの健康情報の権限やプライバシーポリシーの確認では代えられません。同じアカウントの別の端末で記録を続けて見たり復元したりするため、薬の名前、注射予定と投与記録、体重などの身体の測定値、食事・たんぱく質、症状とメモを処理します。記録は端末で暗号化してからサーバーへ送ります。同期の利用中は保管し、ストアが確認した最後のPlus期間の終了から30日後に削除します。削除前に定期購入を再確認し、ストアに障害がある場合は最大7日遅れることがあります。直接削除したり同意を撤回したりした場合、この待機期間は適用しません。同意しなくても端末の記録機能は使えますが、健康情報の同期は利用できません。既存の端末の記録を含めるかどうかは別に選べます。

公開のお知らせはアプリ起動時、オンボーディングより先に確認できます。お知らせごとの「1週間表示しない」はこの端末に保存されます。接続時にIPアドレスなどが処理されることがあります。ウェブサーバーは、IPアドレス、時刻、要求されたアドレス、応答の状態とサイズ、参照元、ブラウザーまたはアプリの識別情報（ユーザーエージェント）をアクセスログとして最長11日間保存します。このリクエストもCloudflareを経由します。国外移転の詳細はプライバシーポリシーに記載しています。

sections.title: 2. 端末に保存する情報
paragraphs: DoseWeekは、ユーザーが手動で入力・確認した以下の情報をアプリ専用領域に保存します。このポリシーで説明する任意の連携、バックアップ、書き出しを除き、情報はアプリ機能の提供に限りAndroid端末上で処理されます。
items: 製品・地域、用量、曜日、時刻、タイムゾーン基準を含む週1回の注射スケジュール
日付、時刻、用量、選択した注射部位、任意のメモを含む実際の投与記録
ユーザーがスキップとして記録した週次予定
残りの投与回数として管理する在庫数
ユーザーが手動で入力した体重と腹囲
症状、程度、時刻、任意のメモを含む副作用の記録と、入力した理由を含む投与記録の修正・削除の変更履歴
ユーザーが選んだ設定：アクセントカラーと外観、リマインダーの文言に薬の名前を表示するかどうかを含むリマインダー設定、アプリロックのオン・オフ

sections.title: 3. 任意のサービスと利用状況分析
paragraphs: DoseWeek 1.0.6は既定の状態で以下の機能や自動処理を使用しません。すべての記録はユーザーが手動で入力・確認します。

この内容は2026年10月3日から適用されます。アカウント、同期、Plus、広告などの新機能に関する部分は、これらの機能を最初に備えるDoseWeekのバージョン(1.0.6)について説明しており、そのバージョンの公開時から適用されます。それより前のバージョンにこれらの機能はありません。

AppleまたはGoogleでDoseWeekアカウントに任意でログインできます。ログインしなくても従来の端末内記録機能を使えます。いずれかのストアで確認済みのPlusを同じアカウントに連携すると、両方のプラットフォームで暗号化同期を利用できます。確認済みのPlusなら、広告の非表示とPlusの機能も両方のプラットフォームで利用できます。Appleの連携を解除するため、サーバーはAppleの更新トークンを別のサーバー鍵で暗号化して保管する場合があります。健康記録のエンドツーエンド暗号化鍵とは異なります。

別途有効にすると、すべての記録（注射計画とその変更、投与記録、食事、身体の測定値、在庫、取り込み履歴）と対応する設定を端末上で暗号化し、両プラットフォームの間で自動バックアップと同期を行います。同期する設定は、外観（カラーとライト・ダークモード）、体重変化の単位、ボディマップの表示方法、注射リマインダーのオン・オフ、通知に詳細や薬の名前を表示するかどうか、計画なしで記録だけを行うかどうか、在庫の追跡、食品検索の地域と検索言語の選択です。別の端末でこれらの設定を変更すると、この端末にも適用し、リマインダーや在庫の追跡などの重要な変更は一度お知らせします。同期によってAI機能がオンになることはなく、端末ごとにご自身でオンにします。通知の許可、アプリロック、健康データ・カレンダー・クラウドストレージとの連携、ウィジェットの外観は端末ごとに決める項目で、同期しません。設定から復元すると、保存されていた設定を適用し、どの設定が変わったかをお知らせします。これはエンドツーエンド暗号化です。サーバーに残るのは暗号化されたスナップショットと、必要なアカウント・購入の記録だけです。データ鍵は復旧コードでロックした形でのみ保存され、復旧コードは利用者の端末にだけあるため、運営者も健康記録を読めません。サーバーはアカウントとログイン事業者の識別子、確認済みPlus状態、暗号文、版情報と最小限のアクセス情報を扱いますが、読める健康記録や復旧コードは受け取りません。新しい端末では復旧コードが必要です。紛失すると開発者も復元できません。空の端末はコードの確認後に復元を始められますが、記録のある端末では事前確認と統合の承認が必要です。ストアで購読状態を再確認するため、サーバーは購入識別子の鍵付きダイジェストと、Appleの元の取引IDまたはストア購入トークンを含む暗号化された照会参照も保存します。参照は健康記録のエンドツーエンド暗号化鍵とは別のサーバー専用鍵でAES-256-GCM暗号化し、ストア確認にのみ使用します。アカウント削除時に参照を消去し、期限切れの参照は30日後に削除します。購入の重複連携を防ぐための鍵付きダイジェスト標識は、韓国の「電子商取引等における消費者保護に関する法律施行令」第6条に基づく代金決済および財貨等の供給に関する記録として5年間保管し、その後削除します。AI記録アシスタント（Pro）に同意して送信した内容は、エンドツーエンド暗号化の例外です。この内容は、回答を作成している間、DoseWeekサーバーとGoogleが読み取れます。Googleは、保持している間もこの内容を読み取れます。保持期間はメモリ上で最大24時間、不正利用検知で疑いがあると判定されたリクエストは最大90日間で、その場合は権限のあるGoogleの担当者が確認することがあります。

利用統計とその国外移転には、それぞれ別の任意の同意が必要です。ログイン、同期、広告の選択とは別です。どちらかを拒否すると統計は無効のままで、基本機能は利用できます。健康記録や復旧コードを統計に送りません。

公開のお知らせはアプリ起動時、オンボーディングより先に確認できます。お知らせごとの「1週間表示しない」はこの端末に保存されます。接続時にIPアドレスなどが処理されることがあります。ウェブサーバーは、IPアドレス、時刻、要求されたアドレス、応答の状態とサイズ、参照元、ブラウザーまたはアプリの識別情報（ユーザーエージェント）をアクセスログとして最長11日間保存します。このリクエストもCloudflareを経由します。国外移転の詳細はプライバシーポリシーに記載しています。

必須のプライバシー通知を確認しても、分析を許可したことにはなりません。利用状況の分析と国外移転にそれぞれ別途同意した場合のみ、分析が有効になります。両方の任意の選択は初期状態でオフになっており、いずれかを拒否または撤回すると分析は無効になります。

利用状況分析は任意で、初めはオフです。必須のプライバシー通知を確認しても、分析への同意にはなりません。別途許可した後にだけ Google Analytics for Firebase が起動し、初回起動、セッション、利用頻度、利用時間、アプリやOSの更新など、自動的なライフサイクル・技術イベントを Google に送信します。開発者は利用状況の把握にレポートを使います。DoseWeek は独自のイベントを追加しません。

分析には Firebase が生成するアプリインスタンス・インストール識別子、イベント時刻、アプリのバージョン、言語、端末のブランド・モデル・種類、マイナーバージョンを含むOS情報、画面解像度が含まれる場合があります。Google はサービス運用と都市などのおおよその位置の推定にIPアドレスを処理します。都市から導出される座標は利用者のGPS位置ではありません。分析にGPSや位置情報の権限は使いません。Google は国外を含む可能性のある自社サーバーで処理し、開発者はレポートを閲覧できます。これらの記録は、それ自体が匿名情報というわけではありません。

DoseWeek は健康記録、薬名、用量、メモ、文字・音声入力、画面名や経路を分析に送りません。ユーザーIDや独自のユーザー属性を設定しません。広告ID・Android ID (SSAID)の収集、自動画面レポート、Google シグナル、広告のパーソナライズは無効です。Crashlytics と Performance Monitoring は使いません。

Google Analytics のユーザー・イベント単位の保存期間は2か月で、新しいアクティビティによる期間のリセットはオフです。設定変更は24時間後に反映され、期限を過ぎたデータは2か月ちょうどの時点ではなく Google の月次処理で削除されます。この設定は標準の集計レポートには適用されず、その永久的な提供を保証するものではありません。

匿名の月別合計の長期保存は、識別を防ぐプライバシー審査と検証済みの書き出しを経た後にのみ計画しています。実際のデータでこの書き出しを行ったことはまだなく、分析の元データを匿名情報として扱いません。

Google LLC — 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, CA 94043, USA. Googleのデータ保護に関するお問い合わせ：https://privacy.google.com/businesses/processorsupport

任意のアプリ利用状況分析、統計レポートの提供、および当該サービスの運営のための委託処理・保管です。広告やパーソナライズには使用しません。

分析データの収集・利用と国外移転の両方に同意して分析を有効にすると、アプリの利用中にFirebase Analytics SDKがHTTPS経由で収集センターにデータを送信し、その後Google Analyticsの処理サーバーに転送されます。送信は非同期で行われる場合があります。

国外移転の可能性がある範囲（2026年9月23日時点の公開情報に基づく）：Argentina, Australia, Austria, Belgium, Brazil, Canada, Chile, Colombia, Croatia, Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, India, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Japan, Kenya, Malaysia, Mexico, Netherlands, Norway, Peru, Philippines, Poland, Portugal, Singapore, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand, Turkey, United Arab Emirates, United Kingdom, United States, Uruguay。これは、Googleの規約で認められる施設所在国での処理と、Googleが公開する施設および該当サービスのサブプロセッサの一覧に基づく範囲です。利用者ごとの固定された経路や、すべての国への移転を示すものではありません。施設一覧には開発中の施設も含まれ、サブプロセッサの国は法人の所在地を示します。同意を得た移転先の国や受領者などの事項を変更する場合は、お知らせしたうえで別途同意を求めます。

PIPA Article 28-8(1)(1)

https://datacenters.google/locations/

https://business.safety.google/adssubprocessors/

利用状況分析への同意は、任意の食品ラベル認識と別途開示された Google ML Kit の指標への同意とは別です。一方の選択を変更しても他方は変わりません。

Health Connect連携は読み取り専用です。DoseWeekは、ユーザーが共有した体重、身長、体脂肪率、除脂肪体重を読み取るだけで、書き込みや削除の権限を要求しないため、他のアプリが所有する記録を変更できません。読み取った情報はアプリ専用領域に保存され、開発者が読める形では送信されません。ほかの記録と同様に暗号化バックアップに含まれ、アカウント同期をオンにした場合は、取得元と非表示の選択とともにエンドツーエンド暗号化された同期コピーにも含まれます。開発者はこのコピーを読めません。Health Connectから読み取った情報はAI機能にも使用せず、AI記録アシスタントにも送信しません。
Googleドライブ連携をオンにすると、アプリは暗号化されたバックアップをユーザー自身のGoogleドライブのアプリデータフォルダへアップロードできます。開発者は複製も鍵も保持しません。ドライブから見える情報と復旧コードの扱いは第4項で説明します。

カレンダー連携をオンにすると、DoseWeekは選択した1つのカレンダーに、今後の注射予定日ごとにタイトルと時刻だけを含む30分の予定を書き込みます。タイトルは既定で「個人的なリマインダー」で、説明付きのタイトルを自分で選んだ場合にのみ「注射予定日」になります。薬の名前、用量、注射部位、メモは決して書き込みません。アプリはカレンダーの一覧と自分が目印を付けた予定だけを読み、その予定だけを更新または削除します。カレンダーがGoogleやSamsungなどのアカウントに属する場合、そのプロバイダーが自身のプライバシーポリシーに従って予定を保存・同期し、カレンダーを共有している相手にも表示されることがあります。開発者は何も受け取りません。連携をオフにすると今後の予定を削除でき、アプリをアンインストールした後にカレンダーに残った予定はそのまま残ります。
